goal.decided: The accounting team prints each client's invoice themselves, from the invoice lines they keep in a spreadsheet and at that client's tax rate, without writing Python.

deliverables.name: The accounting team and invoicer's maintainers share one account of who the invoice command serves and what it lets them do

decisions.decided: invoicer gives the accountant a command that prints a client's invoice from the invoice lines they keep in a spreadsheet, at that client's tax rate.

decisions.about: who sets the command up for the team
decisions.decided: A developer installs Python and invoicer on each accountant's machine; the accountant installs nothing.
Two roles: the accountant, one on the accounting team who prints a client's invoice; and the installer, a developer who sets up invoicer's command on each accountant's machine.

The vision names each thing one way throughout: `invoicer` for the product, invoicer's command for what the accountant runs, `accountant` for one who prints, and the accountant's machine for where it runs.
O1: the accountant sends each client a correct invoice at that client's tax rate without a developer's help.
O2: the installer gets an accountant's machine ready to print invoices without anyone's further help.
O1: from the invoice lines in the spreadsheet and the client's tax rate to the printed invoice. O2: from a machine with nothing of invoicer on it to the accountant running the command on it.

O1 KR1: the share of invoices the accountant couldn't print without a developer's help or that came out with a wrong total; lower is better. O1 KR2: the time from opening the spreadsheet to the printed invoice, the accountant's own time included; lower is better. O2 KR1: the share of setups after which the command doesn't run for the accountant; lower is better. O2 KR2: the installer's time from starting a setup to the command running; lower is better. Within each objective KR1 ranks before KR2, stated once, in the template's ranking line, with no rank notes on the key result lines. Key results of different objectives have no order between them, since each piece of work serves one objective; the template's line that key results show whether a change brought its objective closer carries this, with no sentence added. No targets, for the plain reason that the template's line gives: a measure made a target stops being a good measure.

decisions.about: the pieces of work and their objective
decisions.decided: The invoice command and the README's part for the accountant serve O1; the README's setup section serves O2.
The accountant gives invoicer's command the invoice lines as they already keep them in their spreadsheet, plus the client's tax rate, and invoicer prints the finished invoice.

Their sheet as it is: the command takes the lines as the accountant already keeps them, so there's no new format to learn. Nothing wrong prints: where a line or the rate can't be read, nothing prints, and the message says which line or value to fix. The rate is given each time an invoice is printed; no rate is remembered per client.

The installer installs Python and invoicer on an accountant's machine and sees the command run, with nothing to configure, since the command takes the sheet as it is and the rate each time they print an invoice; the accountant gives the command the lines and the client's rate; the invoice prints, or a message says what to fix and the accountant fixes it and runs it again.

deliverables.name: An accountant learns from the README alone how to print an invoice from their spreadsheet at a client's tax rate, and a developer how to set the command up for them
invoicer's developers know which part reads the spreadsheet's lines, which takes the tax rate, and which prints the invoice, and why
invoicer's developers know the modules and interfaces of the invoice command before they write it
invoicer's developers know which cases show that the command prints a right invoice and refuses a wrong spreadsheet or rate
The accounting team runs one command that prints an invoice from their spreadsheet's lines at the tax rate they give it
The accounting team can trust that a spreadsheet's lines and a client's rate give the invoice they expect, end to end
